conflicts.question: Which side owns the listing rail?

evidence.claim: The base listing grid has direction:ltr and first column 240px; this rule is superseded for the target listing.
The later .listing-page .listing-layout rule sets direction:rtl and the effective flexible rail columns.
The prior FilterSelect board deliberately left page-level rail placement out of scope.

conflicts.resolution: Follow S4: in the Persian RTL listing, the first grid column and filter rail occupy the right side.

conflicts.question: Is the mobile filter surface a bottom sheet or centered dialog?

evidence.claim: The final overlay aligns items and content at the center; the dialog is width 358px and height 756px at 390x844.
Earlier base declarations described bottom alignment; later rules override them.

conflicts.resolution: Preserve the effective centered dialog and animate a small vertical lift with a fading backdrop.

conflicts.question: Which separator token should the rail reference use?

evidence.claim: The current listing rail uses --nova-ref-line: rgb(83 61 46 / 13%).
The prior FilterSelect handoff normalized line/200 to #E4DCD5.

conflicts.resolution: Use the live component token value rgb(83 61 46 / 13%) because it is directly consumed by the current rail.

conflicts.question: How large must the mobile dialog close and reset controls be?

evidence.claim: The late mobile dialog rule sets the close icon target to 32px and the listing reset link to 27px.
Customer mobile controls require at least 44 by 44 CSS-pixel targets.

conflicts.resolution: Use 44 by 44 CSS pixels for the close control and at least 44px height for the reset link; keep the visible close glyph compact.
